notes:
Context: CodeCraft Copilot is building a JetBrains (IntelliJ / PyCharm) plugin that combines local code indexing with a lightweight on-device LLM for completions and a Redwood-hosted fallback. They want a deterministic dev experience: low-latency streaming completions (<100ms median), per-project model/version pinning, and explicit controls to keep repo symbols off-host unless customer opts in.

POC ask: integrate Redwood SDK into their plugin, demonstrate local quantized model path + streaming token by token completion in the IDE, provide telemetry-free local indexing option, and show routing policy: local -> dedicated -> hosted fallback. POC duration 4 weeks.

Security & compliance: enterprise customers require SSO/SAML, audit logs, KMS integration for workspace keys, retention controls, and EU data residency for some accounts. Legal raised questions about on-prem licensing terms and export controls for certain quantized runtimes.

Quotes / highlights: "We need completions to feel instant inside IntelliJ — developers will drop it if latency is >100ms." — Lead Eng (A. Gupta).

Business case: targeted customers are developer teams inside mid-market SaaS companies; revenue model is per-seat + dedicated capacity for enterprise on-prem installs. Estimated ARR if successful across pilot customers: $50k–$150k/year.

Notes from call: security questionnaire sent (see Drive), FE team to run local indexing memory profile on two monorepos, SE to instrument sample plugin with timestamped events for median/95th latency. Next demo scheduled after SSO test.

Stubs: pricing deck (drive link above), security FAQ (drive link), initial plugin prototype in private repo (access pending).
